significance: A hilltop shrine near the Nilagiri hills named for the five Shivalingas set inside it, over which a perennial stream runs and continuously bathes them. Worshippers lie flat on the rock beside the stream to reach and touch the lingas in their natural basin.
story: One account credits Sita with installing the lingas during the exile; another says the asura king Banasura worshipped these self-manifested lingas here for the beauty of the place.
